case_title: Anjani Kumar Chaudhary v. State of Bihar
aggravating_circumstances: Open declaration of intent to kill, use of deadly weapons, multiple attackers
trial_court_outcome: Discharged, case transferred to Chief Judicial Magistrate
high_court_outcome: Affirmed the order of the Court of Session
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused, a practicing advocate, was sitting in the house of an acquaintance when several persons arrived and demanded Rs. 1000 as Rangdari for Holi expenses. The accused gave Rs. 200 but refused to pay the full amount. Approximately 12 persons, including the accused, arrived with weapons and assaulted the accused, causing injuries. The accused was admitted to the hospital and a criminal case was registered. The trial court discharged the accused, transferring the case to the Chief Judicial Magistrate. The High Court affirmed the order. The Supreme Court reviewed the case, noting the open declaration of intent to kill and the use of deadly weapons, and set aside the previous orders, leading to the accused being convicted of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
